narr: Intense thunderstorm clusters tracked north into the Piney Woods of Deep East Texas near an instability gradient along and northeast of a warm front that was slowly shifting northward from the coast. With precipitable water values approaching 2 inches, training thunderstorms resulted in daily rainfall amounts exceeding 4 inches in some locations with the city of Lufkin being the primary location for urban flooding during the early evening hours on May 12th.
ev: Several country roads flooded across Angelina County including FM Road 324, 843 and 706. Several Lufkin city streets also flooded, including a bridge washout on Wilton Street off of Paul Avenue.
lsr: Several county roads underwater across Angelina County including FM 324, 843 and 706. Several city streets also with high water including a report of a bridge washout at Wilton Street off of Paul Ave
